A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the community structure and composition of zooplankton can be affected by the pH history of lakes and that zooplankton are adapted to historical pH conditions in boreal shield region lakes.
zooplankton species in acid-recovering Carlyles Lake have adapted to the historical low pH and that this adaptation has been retained after the lake-water pH has recovered.

the zooplankton of the historically acidified lake were better adapted to low pH, and this was reflected in their greater survival, establishment and abundance at low pH in the reciprocal transplant experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acid-tolerant zooplankton species are more abundant in acidified lakes and that zooplankton are adapted to historical pH in acid-recovering lakes.

there is no one-size fits all approach to lake acidification recovery and that local environmental characteristics and ecological history are important factors to consider when predicting community responses to environmental change.
zooplankton can be adapted to historical acidification, and this adaptation may be important for community structure and recovery.
